Lessons.Title: Funding the Future
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Create a polynomial to model a simple investment situation. Generalize the structure of integers in order to see similarities to polynomials.

Repeated yearly deposits produce a polynomial in an unspecified growth multiplier r. After three equal deposits of 1000, a simple end-of-year model is P(r)=1000(1+r+r^2); check each deposit timing. Positional representation parallels place value: digits weighted by powers of 10.

Source activity 2.1: Notice and Wonder: Writing Numbers: What do you notice? What do you wonder? 3 100s, 2 10s, 9 1s \(3(10^2) + 2(10^1) + 9(10^0)\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 2.2: Polynomials in the Integers: Consider the polynomial function \(p\) given by \(p(x)=5x^3+6x^2+4x\). Evaluate the function at \(x=\text-5\) and \(x=15\). How does knowing that \(5,\!000+600+40 = 5,\!640\) help you solve the equation \(5x^3+6x^2+4x=5,\!640\)? \(11^2 = 121\) and \((x+1)^2 = x^2 + 2x +1\) \(11^3 = 1331\) while \((x+1)^3 = x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1\) The digits in the powers of 11 correspond to the… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 2.3: A Yearly Gift: At the end of 12th grade, Clare’s aunt started investing money for her to use after graduating from college four years later. The first deposit was \$300. If \(r\) is the annual interest rate of the account, then at the end of each school year the balance in the account is multiplied by a growth factor of \(x=1+r\). After one year, the total value is \(300x\). After two years,… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Select all polynomial expressions that are equivalent to \(6x^4+4x^3-7x^2+5x+8\). \(6x^5+4x^4-7x^3+5x^2+8x\) \(6x^4+4x^3-7x^2+5x+8\) \(8+5x+7x^2-4x^3+6x^4\) \(8+5x-7x^2+4x^3+6x^4\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Each year a certain amount of money is deposited in an account which pays an annual interest rate of \(r\) so that at the end of each year the balance in the account is multiplied by a growth factor of \(x=1+r\). $500 is deposited at the start of the first year, an additional $200 is deposited at the start of the next… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Consider the polynomial function \(p\) given by \(p(x)=5x^3+8x^2-3x+1\). Evaluate the function at \(x=\text-2\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: An open-top box is formed by cutting squares out of a 5 inch by 7 inch piece of paper and then folding up the sides. The volume \(V(x)\) in cubic inches of this type of open-top box is a function of the side length \(x\) in inches of the square cutouts and can be given by \(V(x)=(7-2x)(5-2x)(x)\). Rewrite this… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: A rectangular playground space is to be fenced in using the wall of a daycare building for one side and 200 meters of fencing for the other three sides. The area \(A(x)\) in square meters of the playground space is a function of the length \(x\) in meters of each of the sides perpendicular to the wall of the daycare… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Tyler finds an expression for \(V(x) \) that gives the volume of an open-top box in cubic inches in terms of the length \(x\) in inches of the square cutouts used to make it. This is the graph Tyler gets if he allows \(x\) to take on any value between -1 and 7. What would be a more appropriate domain for Tyler to use… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Edulytics independent cool-down: Write the accumulation polynomial for 200 deposited at the end of each of four years; evaluate at r=1. Expected reasoning or answer: 200(1+r+r^2+r^3); at r=1 total 800.
